title: T2: Cap Vitest workers and add process-tree memory measurement
description:
AUDIT REFERENCE: section 2 (OOM assessment), recommendations R1 and R7.

EXISTING
vitest.config.ts sets only `include`. Everything else is Vitest 5 defaults, so
maxWorkers = os.availableParallelism() = 20 on the primary agent host
(20 CPU, 7,790 MB RAM, 2,048 MB swap already 91% consumed at idle).

MEASURED
Process-tree peak RSS: 3,051 MB @ 1 worker, 4,116 MB @ 4, 4,897 MB @ 6.
Wall clock: 181 s @ 1, 55 s @ 4, 48 s @ 6.
Projected >= 13 GB at the default, against a ~9.8 GB RAM+swap envelope. The
default was deliberately never executed.
Parallelism past ~6 buys nothing: the run is latency-bound on
contextAssembler.test.ts. The default costs ~3x the memory for ~0 wall-clock
gain -- strictly worse on both axes, with no trade-off to weigh.

REQUIRED WORK

1. Cap workers in vitest.config.ts. Use an ABSOLUTE value, not a percentage,
   so a 20-CPU agent host and a 2-CPU CI runner both land in a measured
   envelope. Suggested: maxWorkers: process.env.CI ? 4 : 6. Re-measure and
   adjust from evidence rather than adopting the suggestion unmeasured.

2. Record wall clock and peak memory per verification run.

   CRITICAL -- do NOT use /usr/bin/time -v for memory. Its "Maximum resident
   set size" is getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) ru_maxrss, the peak RSS of the
   LARGEST SINGLE CHILD, never the sum across concurrently live children.
   Verified on the agent host: three concurrent children at ~448 MB each
   (~1.34 GB aggregate) reported 458,656 KB.

   Applied to this suite it would report ~2.5 GB while the process tree is at
   4.9 GB, and would show NO difference between the 4- and 6-worker configs
   whose aggregate peaks differ by ~780 MB -- reassuring numbers in exactly
   the scenario that causes the OOM.

   Use instead:
   - sample the run's process group at ~1 Hz (ps -e -o pgid=,rss= with the run
     launched under setsid) and record the peak sum; or
   - read cgroup v2 memory.peak for the run's cgroup, which is exact and
     cannot miss a spike between samples. GitHub-hosted runners expose
     cgroup v2.

   /usr/bin/time -v remains fine for WALL CLOCK and for single-process steps
   (typecheck, format) where largest-child and tree totals coincide.

ACCEPTANCE
- maxWorkers is capped absolutely and the chosen value is justified by a
  recorded measurement on at least two worker counts.
- Memory instrumentation reports aggregate process-tree or cgroup peak, and
  its correctness is demonstrated (a run whose reported peak tracks the tree,
  not the largest child).
- Wall clock and peak memory are recorded per CI verification run and
  retained as an artifact.
- The authoritative gate still runs the full suite. No test is excluded.

EXCLUSIONS
No suite partitioning here (audit T4/R3, not materialized). No isolate:false
-- the audit measured only ~4.93 s available there and it trades away
per-file module-registry isolation several suites rely on.

FOLLOW-ON
Once this lands, re-examine eshyra-da8d and eshyra-5g3d. Both are
load-dependent timeouts whose cause this makes deterministic; eshyra-da8d was
previously treated by raising a timeout budget (commit 473424d), which is the
symptom layer.
